illustrations.alt: An engraved view down a long archive corridor: tall shelving bays of bound ledgers, boxes, rolled maps and card drawers recede to a vanishing point, and a few thin green dotted lines join items on opposite sides of the aisle.
illustrations.caption: The record already holds more than anyone has read across. The lines mark connections between items that sit far apart on the shelves.

illustrations.alt: An engraving of a long reading room filled wall to wall with stacks of bound volumes, tied bundles of paper and document boxes; above them a lattice of fine straight lines joins the stacks in pairs, one line drawn in green, over a small empty reading table.
illustrations.caption: Every new artifact can pair with every one already there. The possible pairs outgrow the reading.

illustrations.alt: An engraved cross-section of ground whose strata are compressed layers of paper, books and index cards, with a sealed scroll, a tied bundle, an index card, a corroded gear, a corked bottle and a leaf embedded at different depths; one green line runs between the scroll and the leaf.
illustrations.caption: Each piece is on the record. The connection between pieces in different layers is not.

illustrations.alt: A specimen plate of six objects laid out like catalogued finds: an open card-catalog drawer of blank index cards, a cubic crystal model, a glass medicine bottle with capsules, a corroded gear fragment, a folded sheet with a lens diagram and a tied scroll; a green thread runs from an index card through the crystal model to the bottle.
illustrations.caption: The excavations run through library cards, materials, medicine, mechanisms and archives.

illustrations.alt: An engraved excavation trench laid out with a string grid on wooden stakes, with books and paper stacks emerging from the soil in several squares; along the edge lie finds trays, a trowel, a brush, dividers, a sieve, a plumb bob and a closed notebook, and one boundary string is green.
illustrations.caption: A discipline sets its boundary first, then records what it finds and what it rejects.
